chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And they ask you about what they should spend. Say: The spare (al-'afw).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The spare is the middle (moderate amount).'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic term 'al-'afw' mean in the context of charitable spending?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interprets the term 'al-'afw' in Surah Al-Baqarah as 'the middle way,' establishing a theological principle of moderation (*wasatiyyah*) in financial conduct. This explanation aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on avoiding the extremes of extravagance and miserliness, thereby framing charity as a balanced act of worship that sustains both the giver and the community.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [2:219] And they ask you as to what they should spend. Say: Whatever you can spare. Heasws said: ‘The ‘spare’, is the middle (neither too little nor too much)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from certain individuals of his people who has said the following:

“About the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, ‘They ask you about what should spend (for the sake of Allah). Say, “It is disregarding. . .’” (2: 219), Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘The word “al-‘Afw (disregarding)” refers to spending moderately.’”
